title.narrative: Activity under preparation EU India Global Partnerships

description.narrative: India is a key strategic partner for the EU and its Member States. Supporting sustainability in third countries is a key dimension of the Global Gateway and considered mutually beneficial by both the EU and India. India has been providing development assistance in bilateral and trilateral modes to countries beyond its neighbourhood, including Africa, the Caribbean and the Americas. The EU has been supporting two international organisations set up by India ¿ the International Solar Alliance (ISA) and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI). Both these organisations have been identified as critical partners to expand the EU¿India strategic partnership globally.In June 2025, the EU and India committed to jointly invest in projects that foster economic growth, job creation, and sustainable development in third countries by signing an Administrative Agreement on Trilateral Cooperation. At the 16th India-EU Summit held in January 2026, ¿Towards 2030: A Joint India-European Union Comprehensive Strategic Agenda¿ was adopted by both partners. It reiterates the importance of ¿promoting cooperation in third countries¿ through trilateral cooperation projects, in areas such as energy, climate resilience, green mobility, and digitalisation. The strategy also aims to strengthen engagement with CDRI for promoting Disaster Risk Reduction, building resilient infrastructure systems in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and least-developed countries (LDCs), as well as increasing cooperation with ISA towards making solar energy technology more accessible and affordable worldwide.This action aims to deliver on the Joint EU-India Comprehensive Strategic Agenda and the Global Gateway in third countries, in the framework of the UN 2030 Agenda and the Paris Agreement, pursuing two specific objectives: Strengthen EU-India trilateral cooperation partnership, with a particular focus on sustainable transport, clean energy, digital and green transition including from a human rights-based and gender equality approach. Strengthen EU-ISA trilateral cooperation and ISA¿s Solar Technology Application Research Centre (STAR-C) programme in third countries.
